content.glance: In a winding up, workmen's dues and debts due to secured creditors, to the extent the section ranks them, are paid in priority to all other debts.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 326 (Overriding preferential payments). In a winding up, workmen's dues and debts due to secured creditors, to the extent the section ranks them, are paid in priority to all other debts. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: In a winding up, workmen's dues and debts due to secured creditors, to the extent the section ranks them, are paid in priority to all other debts.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The section must be read with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code where the process is a Code liquidation. The ranking is pari passu between workmen's dues and the secured creditor's relinquished security, in the proportions the section states. It is not a general unsecured preference.
